text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Culturally homogenous research environments have impoverished Swedish research, causing skilled researchers to leave the country and discouraging foreign researchers to come here, writes Ingela Bel Habib, doctor of psychology.

- Government subsidies to political parties will increase by 30 million crowns to 145 million crowns this year, despite large budget cutbacks. The Social Democratic government and its informal partner the Centre Party argue that political parties need more money to inform in adverse times.
- Wine in tetra packs has become a popular item at the state's alcohol monopoly.
- Millions of crowns disappear each year from state funds earmarked for support of new businesses. Authorities vow to step up control.

- Anders Moberg, head of do-it-yourself furniture retail chain IKEA, defends the company's practices which include buying low-priced goods from developing countries. Trade is better than aid, he says. By establishing business relationships with these countries, the company can have a positive effect on working environment and production methods, Moberg says.

- There is over 13 billion crowns of risk capital which is waiting to be invested despite the fact that the amount invested in new companies rose sharply last year. The main reason is that there are too few entrepreneurs in Sweden.

- Construction and property shares are expected to rise significantly after bottoming out in mid-August, at the earliest, and the index looks like it will break through a resistance level, a technical commentator writes.
